Microsoft breaks ground on Fairwater data center campus in Mount Pleasant

MOUNT PLEASANT, Wis. - Microsoft has begun construction on Fairwater, a data
center campus in Mount Pleasant, Wisconsin, that the company says will draw 900
megawatts at full buildout.

Microsoft first announced the Racine County project in March 2023. The company
has committed $3.3 billion to the site, making it one of the largest single
capital commitments in Wisconsin history.

The first phase, comprising 150 megawatts of capacity, was energized in
January 2026 and is now serving production workloads. Microsoft expects the
remainder of the campus to come online by July 2027.

Microsoft will operate the campus itself and has not announced any third-party
tenants.

The principal obstacle is transmission: American Transmission Company must
complete two 345-kilovolt upgrades before the campus can draw its full load.
Local officials also raised questions about water use for cooling, though the
company has since committed to a closed-loop design.

Construction crews broke ground on the site on 15 June 2023.
